checks.descriptionMarkdown: The crates' names, folders and NSH-free core, from `cargo metadata` (new group).
The macros' crate lookup through `rayx` (new group).

Every crate, test and example compiles against the new names. Whole-workspace on purpose: renaming two crates changes a path in every crate of the workspace, so compiling all of them is this change's focused proof (no test runs).
The core (and the devtools protocol) still build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
release-plz's owner and packages, CI's wasm step and the CLI's library guard name the crates as they are.
The host's source layout (new group).
Every test group of `rayx_app_nsh`. Run whole because the change moves every source file of the crate: this is the owning package's suite, not a workspace run.
No broken intra-doc link in the host after the move.
`StateCell` and `EventStream`: reads, publishes, order, re-entrancy, threads (new group).
Published values as NSH signals and listeners (new group).
`#[contract]`'s shapes and refusals (the macro's unit tests).
Declarations, published state and events, and constants of a TS implementation (new group), with the existing contract group that exercises the same adapter.
Commands and posted members from other threads, on the engine thread, and after the engine stopped (new group).
The engine runner from any thread and after the engine is gone (new group).
Required traits, declared dependencies and lifetimes checked before startup (new group).
`#[contract(ts = …)]` and a RayX class as a contract's token (new group).
A crate's builder method as a class extension, its classes and resolvers from its set; the helpers and the test harness (new group).
`#[app_extension]` as a TS builder method (new group), with the host's group that used `apply(addX)`.
The umbrella's groups that call app extensions, now as builder methods.
The host's four required services in Rust and TS; nothing pre-registered (new group).
The host's existing start groups, whose builders now register the four required services.
The platform, suspension, assets and fonts crates' groups (moved and new).
The storage and navigation crates' groups.
The i18n crate's groups, with the formatter's new group.
The operations, history and selection crates' groups.
The input map and application configuration crates' groups.
The final crate set and the dependency rules, from `cargo metadata` (the `crate_layout` group with its final expectations).
A fake of every core abstraction, used without NSH (new group).
An app's own Rust implementations used by every consumer (new group, every service feature on).
A TS implementation of each of the twelve contracts (new group, every service feature on).
The umbrella's features against `cargo metadata` (new group) and its existing groups under the default features (no `addI18n`).
The umbrella's `native_module` groups with every service feature on (`addI18n` present).
`rayx new`'s services and features (new group), with the CLI groups that check the same files.
The gallery's crate on the new crates.
No file names the old crates or APIs: `git grep` exits 1 when it finds nothing (a match prints it and exits 0, failing the check).
No RayX.Root guide or skill names the old crates or APIs: `git grep` exits 1 when it finds nothing.
The `rayx` skill's files exist and `SKILL.md` opens with `name: rayx` and a description.
argv: import pathlib,re,sys;d=pathlib.Path('.claude/skills/rayx');t=(d/'SKILL.md').read_text(encoding='utf-8');sys.exit(0 if re.match(r'---\r?\nname: rayx\r?\ndescription: \S',t) and (d/'references/services.md').is_file() and (d/'references/contracts.md').is_file() else 1)

checks.descriptionMarkdown: Formatting of the workspace.
Clippy on the touched packages, every target, every feature, warnings denied.

sprints.title: The crates' new names: rayx_app (core) and rayx_app_nsh (host)

tasks.title: Rename rayx_app to rayx_app_nsh, then rayx_core to rayx_app
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Prerequisites (scope): `ts-app-builder` is closed (its `check --epic` and final review), since its checks name today's crates, and RayX pins `nshx-0.5.0-6`. Rename per d-crate-names: `git mv crates/rayx_app crates/rayx_app_nsh` (package, `extern crate self as rayx_app_nsh`), then `git mv crates/rayx_core crates/rayx_app` (package, `extern crate self as rayx_app`); the workspace's members and `[workspace.dependencies]`; every path in every crate, test, example, template and doc comment (`rayx_core::` → `rayx_app::`, the host's `rayx_app::` → `rayx_app_nsh::`); the macros' lookup in `rayx_app_macros/src/lib.rs`; the umbrella (`rayx::app` = core, `rayx::app_nsh` = host, `rayx::core` gone, prelude); `rayx new`'s templates' paths (`rayx::app::app_state()` → `rayx::app_nsh::app_state()`); `release-plz.toml` (owner `rayx_app`, `rayx_app_nsh` added to `changelog_include` with its `[[package]]`), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s wasm step and `ci_workflow.rs` (`-p rayx_app -p rayx_runtime -p rayx_devtools_protocol`), `library_guard.rs`, `release_automation.rs`/`release_config.rs` expectations; `AGENTS.md`'s crate list (names only; the full rewrite is `t19-docs`). New groups: `crates/rayx/tests/crate_layout.rs` (this stage: no `rayx_core`, folders match packages, `rayx_app` NSH-free, `rayx_app_nsh` on `rayx_app`; written so `t13` extends it to the final set) and `crates/rayx/tests/macro_paths.rs`. One `refactor!` commit with the `Migration: apps:` footer of d-crate-names.

sprints.title: The NSH host organized by topic

tasks.title: Move the host's files into app/, di/, configuration/ and services/<name>/
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Move `rayx_app_nsh/src/` to d-layout's table with `git mv` where a file moves whole, splitting `ts/services.rs`, `ts/options.rs` and `platform.rs` by service and keeping each item's docs and tests; `ts/mod.rs` becomes `ts.rs`, re-exporting from the new homes so every public path stays; fix `crate::…` paths and intra-doc links; paths in tests that name source files follow. No behavior change: one `refactor(app): …` commit, no `Migration:` footer. New group `crates/rayx_app_nsh/tests/source_layout.rs`: walks `src/` against the expected tree and names each extra or missing file and folder (written so `t13` can change the expected `services/` to what remains after the split).

sprints.title: Contracts: published values, constants, any-thread calls, class tokens; the core's checks

tasks.title: StateCell and EventStream in the core, and their NSH binding
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Add `StateCell<T>` and `EventStream<E>` to `rayx_app` (next to `ChangeSubscription` in `change.rs`, or a module of their own), exported at the crate root and in its prelude, per d-published-values. In the host's `binding.rs`, a Rust component's signal over a `StateCell` and listener over an `EventStream`, following publishes from any thread on the engine thread (as dXn.Reactive values are today), released with the owner. New groups `crates/rayx_app/tests/published_values.rs` (initial value, publish and get across threads, subscription order, drop stops it, re-entrant read and publish, concurrent publishes, events reaching current subscribers only) and `crates/rayx_app_nsh/tests/nsh_published_binding.rs` (a headless component follows publishes from the engine thread and another thread; stops with its owner).

tasks.title: #[contract]'s shapes: #[state], #[events], #[constant], and TS's ContractState and ContractEvents
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Extend `rayx_app_macros/src/contract.rs` per d-contract-kinds: parse and check the five shapes (refusals list them), generate the trait (commands as `Send` boxed futures), the NSH interface members (state and events as getters of the host's classes, constants as getters) and the adapter: reads state, events and constants once when made, links `ContractState`/`ContractEvents` to its own cells and streams, converts on publish, fails making with a `ContractError` naming a missing constant. Add the `ContractState` and `ContractEvents` classes to the host (`di/contract_ts.rs`) and register them with RayX's TS classes. Command errors take `From<ContractError>` as well as `From<Exception>`. Unit tests in the macro for every shape and refusal; new group `crates/rayx_app_nsh/tests/nsh_tsx_contract_kinds.rs` (declarations text; state before and after publish, from the engine thread and another; subscriber notified once per publish; a bad value throws and keeps the old one; events in order to current subscribers; constants read once, later TS changes unseen, missing constant fails); update `nsh_tsx_contracts` to the new shapes. The `Send` futures' dispatch comes in `t05`; until then the adapter may keep its engine-thread path.

tasks.title: Contracts callable from any thread, and the engine runner
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Per d-any-thread: give each surface a dispatch queue drained by an engine task (NSH wakes the engine from any thread), and the host's `EngineRunner` over it (registered in the surface's root provider). Make the contract adapter's commands and posted members dispatch through it from other threads and spawn directly on the engine thread, awaiting a `futures::channel::oneshot`; close the queue when the engine stops so calls resolve `Err(ContractError::EngineGone { … })`; remove `ContractError::WrongThread` and its uses. New groups `crates/rayx_app_nsh/tests/nsh_tsx_contracts_any_thread.rs` (a command and a posted member from a spawned thread reach the TS implementation; results and thrown errors come back; the engine-thread path skips the queue; a call after the engine stopped resolves `Err`) and `crates/rayx_app_nsh/tests/nsh_engine_runner.rs` (an engine-only NSH call made from another thread; the engine-thread path; after the engine is gone).

tasks.title: Required traits, declared dependencies and lifetimes checked before startup
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Per d-validation, in the core: `ServiceProvider::require::<dyn T>(hint)` and `require_for::<dyn S, dyn T>(hint)` recording requirements (with the requiring registration's lifetime); `RayXAppBuilder::build`/`build_async` check them before any factory, option validation or startup service, collecting every missing trait and every singleton-on-scoped dependency into one `ServiceValidationError` (Display: one line each, who needs what, the hint), and `AppError` gains its variant in the host. New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/di_validation.rs`: a missing required trait, a missing declared dependency, several at once in one error, singleton on scoped, nothing runs before the check fails (a factory and a startup service that record being called), and an app with everything registered building as before. The host's required four and the end of pre-registration come with the service crates (`t09`).

tasks.title: #[contract(ts = …)] and a RayX class as a contract's token
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Per d-contract-tokens: the macro's `ts = "…"` argument names the TS interface; a contract can be given a RayX TS class as its token, so the TS provider treats `addSingletonAs(Class, factory)` and every other registration form under that class as a TS implementation of the contract (registering the adapter as `dyn Trait`, the factory typed by the interface in the declarations), and `getRequiredService(Class)` wraps whichever `dyn Trait` is registered in the class. New group `crates/rayx_app_nsh/tests/nsh_tsx_contract_tokens.rs`, with a contract and a class defined in the test: the interface's name in the declarations; a TS implementation under the class reached from Rust as `dyn Trait` and from TS through the class (state read synchronously); a Rust implementation reached through the same class; a contract without a class keeping its token function.

sprints.title: The host's hooks, then the mandatory four, storage, navigation and i18n as crates

tasks.title: What service crates build on: builder methods as class extensions, app extensions too
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Prerequisite: RayX pins `nshx-0.5.0-6` (scope). Per d-service-crates, give service crates what they build on: public functions an extension method acts on `Instance<RayXAppBuilder>` with, as the builder's own methods do (a Rust registration step, a TS options step through the crate's options class, `AppError::BuilderStarted` once started: today's private `extended`, `add_ts_options` and options steps); a way for a crate's set to register its services' TS classes and resolvers, which the provider uses instead of `RESOLVERS`' fixed list; public helpers for service classes (`ServiceClass`, listeners, options records, `json`); `rayx_app_nsh::testing` behind a `testing` feature with the headless harness of `tests/support` and `tests/headless`. The host's builder keeps its service methods until each service's task moves its method into its crate as a class extension. New group `crates/rayx_app_nsh/tests/nsh_service_crate_hooks.rs` with a service-crate stand-in module in the test (a holder with `#[class_extension(RayXAppBuilder)]`, its own options class, service class and resolver, registered by a set of its own): its method in JS and in `.nsh/types` only with its set; with and without an options callback; a callback that throws; after `start()`; its class resolving through the provider; the harness running a TSX app. Then, per SVC-10, `#[app_extension]` (`rayx_app_macros/src/extension.rs`) generates a class extension of `RayXAppBuilder` in place of its flat TS function: `fn add_weather(builder: RayXAppBuilder) -> RayXAppBuilder` is `builder.addWeather()` in TS, registered by the app's set in the form the macro gives (for example `registry.class_extension::<add_weather>()`, said in its rustdoc); update the groups and docs that call `apply(addX)` (`nsh_tsx_ready`, the umbrella's `native_module` and `native_module_attribute`, `docs/tsx.md`, `docs/services.md`), keeping `apply` for TS functions. New group `crates/rayx_app_nsh/tests/nsh_app_extension_methods.rs` (the method in JS and the declarations with the function's docs; chained with RayX's methods; after `start()` it throws). Two commits: `feat(app): …` for the hooks, `feat(tsx)!: …` for app extensions as builder methods, with `Migration: apps: …`.

tasks.title: Platform, suspension, assets and fonts as crates; the host requires them; nothing pre-registered
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: For each service: define its trait and data types in `rayx_app::services::<name>` (d-abstractions' row; settle the exact members, keeping every capability reachable); create `crates/rayx_services_<name>/` (workspace member, `release-plz.toml` entry, dependencies per d-service-crates) and move RayX's implementation into it as a private type implementing the trait, with its options and `<Name>AppBuilderExt::add_<name>` registering it as `dyn Trait` (and as a startup service under the trait's key when it initializes); move its NSH side and `*_ts.rs` files from `rayx_app_nsh/src/services/<name>/`, make its TS class wrap `Arc<dyn Trait>`, give the contract its class as token (d-contract-tokens), move the service's TS method out of the host's `#[class] impl RayXAppBuilder` into the crate's `#[class_extension(RayXAppBuilder)] impl <Name>Builder` (same TS name, parameters, `#[ts]` and docs), registered by its set's `register(registry)` with its TS classes and resolvers; resolve other services by trait and declare them (`require_for`), removing any registration of another service; replace every consumer's use of the concrete type by `dyn Trait`; move its test groups under their names into `crates/rayx_services_<name>/tests/` (onto `rayx_app_nsh::testing` for NSH ones) and adapt them to the trait; remove what moved from `rayx_runtime` and the host. Commit per service crate (`feat(services)!: …` with `Migration: apps: …`). Services here: platform, suspension, assets, fonts. Also: the NSH asset reader and font registrar become private to their crates and run their NSH calls through the `EngineRunner` (callable from any thread); platform and suspension keep themselves current from their initialization on (what `use_platform_sync`, `keep_platform_current` and the quit wiring did, in Rust and TSX apps alike), and those functions go; fonts resolves `dyn AssetService`; `add_nsh_services`, `NshServicesAppBuilderExt` and the builders' pre-registration go, and the host requires the four (d-validation) in Rust's and TS's start with hints per language. Update the host's start groups to register the four. New group `crates/rayx_app_nsh/tests/nsh_required_services.rs` (each one missing, all missing in one message, Rust and TS, both builders empty when new).

tasks.title: Storage and navigation as crates
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: For each service: define its trait and data types in `rayx_app::services::<name>` (d-abstractions' row; settle the exact members, keeping every capability reachable); create `crates/rayx_services_<name>/` (workspace member, `release-plz.toml` entry, dependencies per d-service-crates) and move RayX's implementation into it as a private type implementing the trait, with its options and `<Name>AppBuilderExt::add_<name>` registering it as `dyn Trait` (and as a startup service under the trait's key when it initializes); move its NSH side and `*_ts.rs` files from `rayx_app_nsh/src/services/<name>/`, make its TS class wrap `Arc<dyn Trait>`, give the contract its class as token (d-contract-tokens), move the service's TS method out of the host's `#[class] impl RayXAppBuilder` into the crate's `#[class_extension(RayXAppBuilder)] impl <Name>Builder` (same TS name, parameters, `#[ts]` and docs), registered by its set's `register(registry)` with its TS classes and resolvers; resolve other services by trait and declare them (`require_for`), removing any registration of another service; replace every consumer's use of the concrete type by `dyn Trait`; move its test groups under their names into `crates/rayx_services_<name>/tests/` (onto `rayx_app_nsh::testing` for NSH ones) and adapt them to the trait; remove what moved from `rayx_runtime` and the host. Commit per service crate (`feat(services)!: …` with `Migration: apps: …`). Services here: storage (its NSH key-value store and the in-memory store, NSH storage calls through the `EngineRunner`, the flush before quitting heard through `dyn SuspensionService`'s events) and navigation (the location synchronizer, regions as NSH navigation stacks, TSX's `NavigationRegion`; the synchronizer seam private to the crate).

tasks.title: I18n as a crate, split into I18nService and MessageFormatter
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: For each service: define its trait and data types in `rayx_app::services::<name>` (d-abstractions' row; settle the exact members, keeping every capability reachable); create `crates/rayx_services_<name>/` (workspace member, `release-plz.toml` entry, dependencies per d-service-crates) and move RayX's implementation into it as a private type implementing the trait, with its options and `<Name>AppBuilderExt::add_<name>` registering it as `dyn Trait` (and as a startup service under the trait's key when it initializes); move its NSH side and `*_ts.rs` files from `rayx_app_nsh/src/services/<name>/`, make its TS class wrap `Arc<dyn Trait>`, give the contract its class as token (d-contract-tokens), move the service's TS method out of the host's `#[class] impl RayXAppBuilder` into the crate's `#[class_extension(RayXAppBuilder)] impl <Name>Builder` (same TS name, parameters, `#[ts]` and docs), registered by its set's `register(registry)` with its TS classes and resolvers; resolve other services by trait and declare them (`require_for`), removing any registration of another service; replace every consumer's use of the concrete type by `dyn Trait`; move its test groups under their names into `crates/rayx_services_<name>/tests/` (onto `rayx_app_nsh::testing` for NSH ones) and adapt them to the trait; remove what moved from `rayx_runtime` and the host. Commit per service crate (`feat(services)!: …` with `Migration: apps: …`). Service here: i18n, split per d-i18n-split: the `I18nService` contract and the Rust-only `MessageFormatter` trait in `rayx_app::services::i18n`; `rayx_services_i18n` with RayX's implementation of both (`add_i18n`, `add_message_formatter`), the formatter's per-language cache dropped on a new version, `tr!`, `checked::tr!` and NSH's locale following the chosen language; RayX's implementation resolves `dyn PlatformInfoService` and `dyn AssetService`. New group `crates/rayx_services_i18n/tests/formatter.rs`: today's formatting results through RayX's implementation; the formatter over a fake `I18nService` (from the test) following a published language change on the next call.

sprints.title: The other services as crates, rayx_runtime gone, replaceability from Rust and TS

tasks.title: Operations, history and selection as crates
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: For each service: define its trait and data types in `rayx_app::services::<name>` (d-abstractions' row; settle the exact members, keeping every capability reachable); create `crates/rayx_services_<name>/` (workspace member, `release-plz.toml` entry, dependencies per d-service-crates) and move RayX's implementation into it as a private type implementing the trait, with its options and `<Name>AppBuilderExt::add_<name>` registering it as `dyn Trait` (and as a startup service under the trait's key when it initializes); move its NSH side and `*_ts.rs` files from `rayx_app_nsh/src/services/<name>/`, make its TS class wrap `Arc<dyn Trait>`, give the contract its class as token (d-contract-tokens), move the service's TS method out of the host's `#[class] impl RayXAppBuilder` into the crate's `#[class_extension(RayXAppBuilder)] impl <Name>Builder` (same TS name, parameters, `#[ts]` and docs), registered by its set's `register(registry)` with its TS classes and resolvers; resolve other services by trait and declare them (`require_for`), removing any registration of another service; replace every consumer's use of the concrete type by `dyn Trait`; move its test groups under their names into `crates/rayx_services_<name>/tests/` (onto `rayx_app_nsh::testing` for NSH ones) and adapt them to the trait; remove what moved from `rayx_runtime` and the host. Commit per service crate (`feat(services)!: …` with `Migration: apps: …`). Services here: operations (a target's handler crosses as a class handle TS can call; transactions as commands on an id; generic `submit::<T>` and friends as helpers on `dyn OperationService`), history (resolves `dyn OperationService`, and `dyn KeyValueStore` for `add_persistent_history`; no longer reads operations' private `instance_id`, which becomes the contract's constant; `HistoryStore` stays public in its crate) and selection (resolves `dyn NavigationService`). `add_history` no longer adds operations, nor `add_persistent_history` storage: they declare them.

tasks.title: Input map and application configuration as crates; rayx_runtime removed; the final crate rules
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: For each service: define its trait and data types in `rayx_app::services::<name>` (d-abstractions' row; settle the exact members, keeping every capability reachable); create `crates/rayx_services_<name>/` (workspace member, `release-plz.toml` entry, dependencies per d-service-crates) and move RayX's implementation into it as a private type implementing the trait, with its options and `<Name>AppBuilderExt::add_<name>` registering it as `dyn Trait` (and as a startup service under the trait's key when it initializes); move its NSH side and `*_ts.rs` files from `rayx_app_nsh/src/services/<name>/`, make its TS class wrap `Arc<dyn Trait>`, give the contract its class as token (d-contract-tokens), move the service's TS method out of the host's `#[class] impl RayXAppBuilder` into the crate's `#[class_extension(RayXAppBuilder)] impl <Name>Builder` (same TS name, parameters, `#[ts]` and docs), registered by its set's `register(registry)` with its TS classes and resolvers; resolve other services by trait and declare them (`require_for`), removing any registration of another service; replace every consumer's use of the concrete type by `dyn Trait`; move its test groups under their names into `crates/rayx_services_<name>/tests/` (onto `rayx_app_nsh::testing` for NSH ones) and adapt them to the trait; remove what moved from `rayx_runtime` and the host. Commit per service crate (`feat(services)!: …` with `Migration: apps: …`). Services here: input map (resolves `dyn KeyValueStore`; `add_input_map` no longer adds storage) and application configuration (resolves `dyn PlatformInfoService`; `add_application_configuration` no longer adds platform). Then remove `crates/rayx_runtime` (workspace member, dependency, re-exports, `release-plz.toml`, CI's wasm step and `ci_workflow.rs`), keeping the name in the CLI's library guard. Extend `crate_layout` to the final set and dependency rules (CRATES-2), and `source_layout` to the host's `services/` after the split (only what service crates build on).

tasks.title: rayx_app::testing's fakes; replacing RayX's implementations from Rust
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Add `rayx_app::testing` with a fake per core trait and of `MessageFormatter` (d-abstractions' invariants; today's `InMemoryKeyValueStore`, `MemoryAssetReader` and the no-op hosts are where they come from), NSH-free. New groups `crates/rayx_app/tests/testing_fakes.rs` (each fake registered as `dyn Trait` in a plain `ServiceProvider`, resolved and used: state published, commands recorded or answered) and `crates/rayx/tests/service_replacement.rs` (every feature: an app's own `dyn AssetService` used by RayX's fonts and i18n, its own `dyn OperationService` by history, its own platform, suspension, assets and fonts satisfying the host's requirement, a service's TS class wrapping the app's implementation).

tasks.title: Each of the twelve contracts implemented in TS
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: New group `crates/rayx/tests/ts_service_contracts.rs` (every feature), one test per contract: a TS class implementing `<Name>Contract`, registered with `addSingletonAs(<Name>, () => new …)` (a startup form where the service initializes), resolved by Rust as `dyn Trait` (published state read synchronously, a command called from the engine thread and from another thread) and by TS through `getRequiredService(<Name>)`; for the services others resolve (assets, operations, navigation, platform, storage, i18n), a RayX consumer working over the TS implementation; the host's requirement satisfied by TS implementations of the four. Fix what the tests find in the contracts, adapters or crates (repair, inside this epic's scope).
